identity.description: Frequent-itemset mining plus rule induction over transaction baskets: finds itemsets whose co-occurrence support clears a floor, then derives antecedent->consequent rules scored by support, confidence, and lift. Emits a per-model RULES table; there is deliberately NO per-row scoring operation.

dtypes: item-ids grouped by transaction-id (collapsed to a boolean transactions x items basket matrix by the wrapper)
consumes.note: consumed as TRANSACTIONS: unordered itemsets keyed by transaction id; timestamps/order in the event-log are dropped by the groupby-collapse

emits.note: the antecedent->consequent rule table with support/confidence/lift/leverage/conviction columns is the ENTIRE output — fitted knowledge, no per-row prediction exists

min_support.note: mlxtend library default is 0.5 — uselessly high for real baskets; there is no supervised objective, so thresholds are governance knobs set by user/agent, not HPO-searchable

algorithm.note: identical results by construction; fpgrowth avoids apriori's candidate-generation memory blow-up

max_len.note: caps itemset length — the combinatorial-explosion guard

min_threshold.note: library default 0.8 (confidence); threshold semantics depend on the chosen metric

invariances.why: input is boolean set-membership; there are no magnitudes anywhere in the counting for a rescale to touch
support/confidence/lift are functions of item PRESENCE counts only; any monotone transform of values upstream leaves membership, and hence every count, unchanged
in a basket matrix an unrecorded item is definitionally FALSE (absent); a literal NaN has no set-membership meaning and indicates a malformed encoding to reject, not handle
items ARE categories — the entire computation is counting over categorical set membership
pure frequency counting; independence appears only as lift's NULL baseline (confidence / expected-confidence-under-independence), never as a fit assumption
support is a proportion over transactions with resolution floor 1/n; a support threshold s is only meaningful when n >> 1/s, else 'frequent' itemsets are one-off coincidences
rules can only cite itemsets actually observed at or above min_support; never-co-occurring combinations are structurally invisible

featureStats.why: support is a proportion with resolution floor 1/n_transactions — below that, any support threshold is counting noise
candidate itemsets grow combinatorially in the number of FREQUENT items; a wide catalog with flat frequencies is the apriori blow-up regime — feeds the max_len and min_support gates
a rule over k items can only be witnessed by baskets holding >= k items; a median basket of 1-2 items makes multi-item rules unminable regardless of thresholds

modelMetrics.why: zero rules means the support/confidence floor sits above the data's co-occurrence density (relax-thresholds signal, not model failure); a >10k explosion means the floor sits below the noise floor
lift = confidence / expected-confidence-under-independence; lift ~= 1 everywhere means co-occurrence is fully explained by item popularity — nothing real was mined

edgeCases.condition: low min_support on a wide item catalog
edgeCases.behavior: combinatorial candidate/itemset explosion; memory blow-up (worst under apriori)
edgeCases.note: bound max_len, raise min_support, prefer fpgrowth / apriori low_memory=True

edgeCases.behavior: empty frequent-itemset table -> empty rules table
edgeCases.note: report honestly or run a bounded threshold-relaxation ladder — never silently return zero rules as success

edgeCases.condition: a staple item present in ~every basket
edgeCases.behavior: high-confidence rules with lift ~= 1 — popularity artifacts, not patterns
edgeCases.note: filter rules by lift/leverage or drop staple items pre-mining

edgeCases.behavior: each distinct value becomes a singleton 'item'; nothing meaningful is minable without discretization

driver.constructor: fpgrowth(basket_df, min_support=..., max_len=...) -> association_rules(frequent_itemsets, metric=..., min_threshold=...) — a two-step mine-then-derive pipeline inside one component's fit
driver.wrapperNeeds: THE defining need: NO SCORING OPERATION. This is a fit-only component — the per-row predict surface does not exist, so the sidecar /predict contract must return the per-model rules artifact (or be disabled) for this component. Wrapper also owns (1) event-log -> boolean basket matrix via TransactionEncoder groupby-collapse, (2) running the two-step fpgrowth->association_rules pipeline in fit, (3) exposing the rules DataFrame as the serialized per-model artifact
driver.threadSafety: single-threaded mining; reading the mined rules table is trivially thread-safe

placementClaims.why: absence IS data: an item not in a basket is False, not missing — a well-formed transactions encoding cannot contain anything to impute (literal NaNs are reject-input upstream)
monotone-transform-invariant by mechanism: only set membership is counted, magnitudes never enter
boolean membership has no scale; standardization is meaningless here
apriori/fpgrowth consume a one-hot boolean transactions x items matrix — the TransactionEncoder collapse from the event-log is mandatory (owned by the wrapper, but structurally an encode)
